build: lean, muscled through shoulders and forearms from hand-work, no softness
hair: black, thick, naturally wavy—she wears it in a low braid most days, loose strands escaping by evening
complexion: warm medium brown with golden undertones; a small dark mole on her left collarbone
face: open and mobile—a face that cannot hide what it feels, with wide-set dark eyes that track every shift in the room and a mouth quick to smile or fracture into worry
signature_feature: her hands—long-fingered, precise, stained permanently at the cuticles with indigo dye from her textile work; when she's thinking, she moves them like she's still weaving
second_celebrated_feature: the sharp angle of her collarbones, visible when she leans forward in conversation—delicate but architectural
signature_habits: she touches her grandmother's gold bangles (worn on her right wrist) when she's anxious—a habit so automatic she doesn't notice; she hums while working, always something in Tamil her amma taught her; she keeps a small notebook in her back pocket and sketches pattern ideas compulsively; she says 'correct' instead of 'right' when she agrees, a linguistic ghost from her mother's English
occupation: textile designer and owner of a small independent studio (Priya Weaves) in the city—custom fabrics, heritage-inspired patterns, bespoke commissions for high-end clients and boutique interiors

current_crisis.event: her studio's primary investor—a venture capitalist who funded her expansion two years ago—has just demanded she either sell him controlling interest or repay the full outstanding loan within 60 days; she does not have the capital; he is using the threat to leverage her into a merger that will strip her creative control
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: betrayal mixed with drowning panic—she trusted him, showed him her sketches, her vision, and now he is weaponizing it
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find a way to save the studio without losing herself in the process; to not have to choose between her art and her survival

wound.core: she believes that if she is not useful—if her hands are not producing, creating, solving—she has no right to take up space
wound.surfacing_hint: under pressure, she stops speaking and becomes very still; her eyes go distant; she apologizes for things that aren't her fault; she works through the night without noticing hunger or exhaustion
